cohort: A 30-year-old woman with a history of curettage, secondary amenorrhea, and infertility due to severe intrauterine adhesions (Asherman's syndrome).
finding: Hysteroscopic adhesiolysis and subsequent treatments can lead to successful pregnancy even in severe cases of Asherman's syndrome, although such pregnancies may be complicated by abnormal placental implantation.
mod_finding: Cesarean section was performed at 39 weeks of gestational age due to low lying placenta, and the delivery was complicated by placenta accreta.
